issuesAndPullRequests.title: Qualify current MCP SDK compatibility foundation
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
Bounded competitive/reuse research refresh, adding the official pinned Python SDK v2.3.0 as an optional transport candidate, not an adopted dependency. Documents current-versus-legacy protocol acceptance, license and measurable comparison gates.

Verification: official release, pinned package/license/README and current protocol sources reviewed. Local source/tests match main 5c215f9; 23 unit tests pass. Actual CLI JSON-RPC rejection followed by successful native discovery verified. Exact research blob read back after upload. No SDK installed, capabilities added, network listener enabled, credentials created, Windows or client acceptance claimed.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Keep discovery usable after invalid optional adapter registration
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
A malformed optional capability could enter the registry with a non-string name and break sorted discovery for every adapter, or reserve an unusable name with a noncallable handler. Validate nonempty string name, callable handler and read/write string effect before mutation. Corrected registration remains possible afterward.

Baseline regression reproduced7 failed assertions/4 errors across invalid registrations. All23 local tests pass, including actual JSON-lines subprocess discovery+diagnostics after rejected optional registrations. Existing Windows/Ubuntu Python3.11/3.13 CI retained. No new adapters, effects, grants, listeners, data access or dependency changes. This is accidental contract validation, not sandboxing trusted Python code or native desktop acceptance.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Recover local transport after malformed UTF-8 lines
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
## Causal repair
A malformed UTF-8 byte under strict stdin decoding previously raised before request handling, terminating the process and losing subsequent buffered valid requests. Explicit UTF-8 surrogateescape decoding retains invalid bytes only until their bounded line is rejected as invalid JSON. Invalid raw bytes never dispatch/echo; valid escaped JSON strings and Unicode identities still work. Existing Unicode-character budget/draining unchanged.

## Evidence
Baseline actual-subprocess regression reproduced UnicodeDecodeError termination. All21 tests now pass locally, including three malformed byte patterns followed by Unicode diagnostics, oversized invalid bytes followed by a valid escaped JSON ID under an ASCII-strict environment, and all prior privacy/adapter independence/serialization regressions. Existing CI tests Python3.11/3.13 on Windows/Ubuntu.

No new adapters, listeners, credentials, permissions, file content access, MCP or dot integration. Hosted OS results pending, not Windows desktop/client acceptance.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Keep optional adapter validation exception text private
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
Handler ValueError/PermissionError previously leaked arbitrary text as trusted request diagnostics. Normalize those failures at the registry handler boundary; preserve registry-owned unsupported/parameter/read-only messages, subsequent diagnostics, OSError handling and shutdown signals.

Two privacy regressions failed before;19tests pass after. Bounded equivalent successful diagnostic timing retained; no speedup claimed. No credentials, listener, persistent grant or native/client acceptance. Hosted CI pending.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Reject duplicate JSON fields before capability dispatch
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
## Regression
Duplicate method/id/params fields silently used their last value and dispatched an ambiguous request. Reject duplicate members at every object depth before dispatch; preserve subsequent valid requests and independent adapters.

## Evidence
Actual subprocess fixture previously called its probe4 times rather than1. All17 tests now pass. Twenty cold diagnostic subprocess samples each: median36.15ms before /34.90ms after on this Linux worker; no speedup claim or Windows acceptance. No safe separate optimization identified.

No network listener, credentials, persistent grant, MCP or dot integration. Hosted CI pending.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Bound diagnostics request memory without losing session recovery
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
The current diagnostics transport read an arbitrarily large line into memory before parsing. Introduce a documented 65,536-character line budget (newline included), drain oversized input using bounded reads, emit one error without dispatching any truncated prefix, and preserve the next complete request.

This is a no-payload transport budget, not a content/catalog cap. Bulk adapters will need a dedicated streaming contract; no new listener/grant/adapter.

Two regression cases fail before. All 16 tests pass after, including real process oversized-to-valid recovery, EOF, exact boundary and instrumentation that every read has a bounded size. CI checks Python3.11/3.13 on Windows/Linux. No native PC or dot acceptance claimed.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Recover local session from invalid adapter output
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
A distinct follow-up to exception isolation: a handler can return successfully but its result can crash JSON serialization (object/cycle), or emit nonstandard NaN/Infinity. Encode fully before writing; replace invalid output with a generic correlated error and continue subsequent diagnostics.

Regression failed before fix. All 13 tests pass locally, including actual subprocess calls returning an unsupported object, cycle, NaN, +/-Infinity then successful diagnostics. No partial response or traceback; no new persistent access, adapters or transport claims. CI validates Linux/Windows Python 3.11/3.13.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Keep diagnostics usable after optional adapter failure
issuesAndPullRequests.body:
## Fix
A RuntimeError in a trusted optional adapter currently terminates the JSON-lines process, breaking later independent diagnostics. Return a generic request-correlated error instead, without exposing arbitrary exception text. KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit remain unswallowed.

## Verification
Two reproductions failed before repair. All 12 local Python tests pass after, including an actual subprocess failed-call → diagnostics → capability-list recovery and shutdown propagation. No network listener, credentials, persistent grants, or new adapter. This is local transport coverage, not dot/MCP/native desktop acceptance. CI checks Linux/Windows Python 3.11/3.13.

issuesAndPullRequests.title: Add independent diagnostics core and source-led computer bridge research
issuesAndPullRequests.body: Implements a deterministic local JSON-line diagnostics foundation with independent capability registry, optional selected-volume capacity, and 8 tests. Adds research/architecture/acceptance docs, real local skill and pinned Agent-Foundry guidance. Live Home wiki created separately and verified. No network listener, grants, desktop installation or actual dot integration configured. This is not MCP or a completed remote-control product. Linux tests passed; hosted Windows/Linux matrix must pass before integration.
